angles: IDE vs CLI: Copilot Agent Mode is IDE-integrated (VS Code), while Codex Cloud is terminal-native — the right choice depends on your primary workflow
Multi-model vs single-model: Copilot lets you switch between GPT, Claude, and Gemini models; Codex is optimized for OpenAI's models
Enterprise vs open-source: Copilot is proprietary with deep GitHub integration; Codex CLI is Apache 2.0 open source
Pricing model comparison: Copilot uses flat monthly subscriptions ($10-$100/user); Codex uses per-token API pricing ($1.50-$6/M tokens)
When to use both: Use Copilot for IDE inline suggestions and chat, Codex for terminal automation and CI/CD pipelines
The convergence trend: Both platforms are adding cloud-based background agents that work autonomously while developers focus on architecture
Terminal proficiency gap: Codex's 77.3% Terminal-Bench score vs Copilot's underlying models (~65%) is the key differentiator for DevOps-heavy teams
Context window trade-off: Copilot (via GPT-5.4) offers 1M tokens; Codex Cloud offers 400K — larger context matters for full-codebase understanding
